2608.01260.title: Auditing Semantic Gains in Sequential Recommendation: A Lightweight Recovery Test
2608.01260.paper_summary: Recent semantic and generative-retrieval recommenders report substantial improvements over ID-only sequential baselines, but it remains unclear whether these gains arise from language-model reasoning, semantic-ID generation, end-to-end semantic architectures, stronger offline item representations, or complementary semantic and collaborative signals. We investigate this attribution ambiguity through LIME-Rec, a lightweight and auditable recovery test. LIME-Rec combines three independent experts: a SASRec sequential expert, an ItemCF co-occurrence expert, and a semantic expert based on frozen BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 item embeddings. Their full-catalog scores are normalized per user and combined through auditable score-level fusion followed by bounded history calibration. The fusion gate and calibration head are fitted on validation data only, require no serving-time language-model inference, and keep each expert contribution separately inspectable. On Amazon Beauty, Toys, and Sports, LIME-Rec achieves R@10 scores of 0.0996, 0.1105, and 0.0593, outperforming the strongest comparison baseline by 7.0%-12.0%. Three-expert fusion without history calibration consistently outperforms calibrated SASRec, showing that calibration alone does not explain the recovery. Randomly permuting item-text embeddings across item IDs reduces R@10 by 13.6%-17.5%, indicating that the gains depend on genuine item-text correspondence rather than additional representation capacity. These results suggest that lightweight recovery from offline item representations and transparent fusion should be ruled out before improvements are attributed to serving-time language modeling, semantic-ID generation, or heavier semantic machinery.
2608.01260.paper_summary_zh: 最近的語義和生成檢索推薦系統報告顯著改善了僅基於ID的序列基準，但仍不清楚這些增益是否源於語言模型推理、語義ID生成、端到端語義架構、更強的離線項目表示，或是互補的語義和協同信號。我們通過LIME-Rec進一步探討這種歸因模糊性，這是一種輕量級且可審計的恢復測試。LIME-Rec結合了三位獨立專家：一位SASRec序列專家、一位ItemCF共現專家，以及一位基於凍結的BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5項目嵌入的語義專家。他們的全目錄分數按用戶進行正規化，並通過可審計的分數級融合進行組合，隨後進行有界歷史校準。融合閘和校準頭僅在驗證數據上進行擬合，無需服務時的語言模型推理，並使每位專家的貢獻可單獨檢查。在亞馬遜的美容、玩具和體育類別中，LIME-Rec的R@10分數分別為0.0996、0.1105和0.0593，超越了最強的比較基準7.0%-12.0%。三專家融合在沒有歷史校準的情況下始終優於經過校準的SASRec，顯示校準本身並不能解釋恢復。隨機置換項目文本嵌入與項目ID之間的關係使R@10降低了13.6%-17.5%，這表明增益依賴於真實的項目文本對應，而非額外的表示能力。這些結果表明，在將改進歸因於服務時的語言建模、語義ID生成或更重的語義機制之前，應排除從離線項目表示的輕量級恢復和透明融合。
